newsitem.title: UK: BA seeks top global cargo role by 2000.
newsitem.headline: BA seeks top global cargo role by 2000.

text.p: British Airways Plc World Cargo wants to be recognised as one of the top players in the global airfreight business by the year 2000, general sales manager and marketing, Paul Giblin said.

He told the cargo division's in-house magazine that one of his key aims "is to create a new mind-set across our network where everyone understands that each consignment should be treated like a passenger who can't hear or speak or see. Unless every piece of freight is given the same care and attention as that passenger, then we won't be successful."
Giblin said that no new products: "would be launched until we've tested it in the market and proved we can deliver it consistently and to a very high standard."

Commenting on suggestions from some in the industry that BA World Cargo cannot be taken seriously until it buys into freighters, Giblin said: "Our first priority is to take what we have and get it working successfully. Once we've done that, I think customers will perceive us very differently and the debate over freighters will hold less weight."
"I believe that we will be able to source enough capacity beyond the belly space of our own aircraft to satisfy customer demand, " he added.

"One way might be to look at creating partnerships with other carriers, but as long as we're able to deliver the goods on a consistent basis, I don't think customers will be so concerned with the manner in which we do it." - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 - www.racs.com
